claim: In multi-agent reinforcement learning for autonomous vehicle lane-changing in mixed traffic, a local reward design yields larger evaluation rewards and smaller variance compared to a global reward design, and this performance advantage increases with the number of vehicles.
falsifier: In a multi-agent RL lane-changing simulator with mixed traffic, compare training curves of agents using local rewards versus global rewards under varying vehicle densities; measure average reward and variance across episodes.

conditions: multi-agent advantage actor-critic (MA2C) framework with parameter sharing
mixed traffic with human-driven vehicles (HDVs) and autonomous vehicles (AVs)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task (lane-changing), traffic modes, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Local reward design versus for larger evaluation rewards
